statuses.label: Announced
statuses.description: A company or public body has publicly announced plans for a service or trial in this place. No public-road testing confirmed yet.

statuses.label: Testing with safety driver
statuses.description: Automated vehicles are being tested on public roads with a trained safety driver on board. No public passengers.

statuses.label: Passenger rides with safety driver
statuses.description: Members of the public (paying, free or pre-registered) can ride, with a safety driver or operator on board.

statuses.label: Driverless testing
statuses.description: Vehicles run on public roads with nobody in the driving seat, as a test (sometimes with invited passengers).

statuses.label: Driverless commercial
statuses.description: A service open to the public with no safety driver on board.

statuses.label: Paused
statuses.description: The operator has temporarily stopped the service.

statuses.label: Ended
statuses.description: The trial or service has finished.

operators.fleetNote: TfL approved Wayve’s modification on up to 15 vehicles on a trial basis (TfL FOI response, Sep 2026)
operators.note: Supervised rides on the Uber app since 3 Sep 2026, with a TfL-licensed private hire driver on board. The service runs under private hire licensing, not the new driverless permit scheme.

sources.label: TfL FOI response FOI-1660-2627, published 4 Sep 2026

operators.operator: Connector (Greater Cambridge Partnership; operated by Whippet, technology from Fusion Processing, Alexander Dennis buses)
operators.fleetNote: “Three cutting-edge buses for passenger trials” (Greater Cambridge Partnership)
operators.note: Free timetabled self-driving bus trials with a trained safety driver on board at all times: from 24 Jun 2025 between Madingley Road Park & Ride, Eddington and Cambridge West, and from 17 Dec 2025 linking Trumpington and Babraham Road Park & Rides with the Cambridge Biomedical Campus. In Aug 2026 the government-funded Commercialising Connector project (£3.88m) was announced to extend the trials. The organisers say services may not run every day.

Autonomous driving with trained specialists behind the wheel since 14 Apr 2026. Waymo said in Oct 2025 that it intends to offer rides with no human behind the wheel in London in 2026, subject to permissions.

operators.operator: Baidu Apollo Go with Freenow by Lyft
operators.note: Road testing of Apollo Go RT6 vehicles with safety operators on board began on 28 Jul 2026, starting in the borough of Brent. The companies plan to welcome public riders from 2027, subject to regulatory approvals.

Uber announced in Dec 2025 that it planned to test Apollo Go vehicles in London. On 28 Jul 2026 Uber said the vehicles were “on the road as we work towards testing and launch”. We have not found a confirmed start date for Uber’s supervised testing, so this stays at Announced.

operators.operator: Nissan (ADventure research project, with WMG at the University of Warwick and PAVE UK)
operators.fleetNote: One specially equipped 2022 Nissan LEAF test car (Nissan)
operators.note: A £3m research project backed by the UK Government’s CAM Pathfinder programme to study how an autonomous passenger mobility service could work in Cambridge, combining real-world testing with community engagement. Nissan says the project will end with a public-road demonstration in Cambridge. No start date for public-road testing has been given.

operators.operator: Oxa (SAMS project led by Sunderland City Council, with Stagecoach)
operators.note: Sunderland Advanced Mobility Shuttle (SAMS): a four-week trial carrying pre-registered public passengers with a safety driver on board, linking Park Lane Interchange and Sunderland Royal Hospital. The trial ended in March 2025.

operators.statusText: Since 10 Sep 2026 (public rides with an operator on board since 8 Apr 2026)
operators.note: Paid public rides with an AV operator on board since 8 Apr 2026 (Verne app), also bookable on the Uber app since 19 Aug 2026. On 10 Sep 2026 Verne and Pony.ai began fully driverless test rides for invited passengers on a 22 km route to Zagreb Airport. The public service still has an operator on board.

operators.operator: MOIA (Volkswagen Group), ALIKE project led by HOCHBAHN
operators.note: Since 15 Jul 2026, selected pre-registered residents can book free shared rides in the self-driving ID. Buzz through the MOIA app, with a trained safety operator on board. The initial area covers parts of Winterhude, Barmbek and Wandsbek. On 27 Sep 2026 heise online, citing WirtschaftsWoche, reported that Volkswagen is examining options for MOIA’s future, from new investors to closure, by the end of 2026. We have not seen an official statement on the Hamburg service.

operators.operator: iamo (Swiss Transit Lab, SBB and the cantons of Zurich and Aargau; technology partner WeRide)
operators.fleetNote: Three passenger cars (iamo); minibuses are planned later
operators.note: Since 28 Sep 2026 members of the public can book paid rides (CHF 4.70 plus CHF 0.38 per km) in the iamo app, daily from 1pm to 5pm, between almost 100 stops in Boppelsen, Dänikon, Hüttikon and Otelfingen. A safety person sits in the driver’s seat. The Federal Roads Office (FEDRO/ASTRA) approved automated driving for the pilot in Nov 2025. Rides without a safety person are planned later with minibuses, subject to FEDRO approval.

sources.label: Canton of Zurich press release, 24 Sep 2026 (German)

operators.operator: Ruter with Holo (vehicles and app from MOIA)
operators.fleetNote: Six Volkswagen ID. Buzz from autumn 2026 (Ruter); the pilot began in late 2023 with five NIO ES8
operators.note: Ruter paused its self-driving pilot from 28 Feb 2026 while new vehicles were brought in. Its project page (updated 16 Sep 2026) says the service will reopen to passengers in September 2026, with a safety operator in the driver’s seat. As of 5 Oct 2026 we have found no announcement that it has restarted.

operators.operator: beti with WeRide (with Renault Group and Macif)
operators.fleetNote: Not officially stated as a number (WeRide: “several” eight-passenger robobuses)
operators.note: A 3.3 km public-road shuttle route between Valence TGV station and the Rovaltain business park, which started on 10 Mar 2025. WeRide called it fully driverless, but France 3 reported in April 2026 that a safety agent was still on board, due to leave the vehicle in early 2027. That report said the current trial phase ran until 4 Apr 2026. Last confirmed in April 2026.

operators.operator: BVG (NoWeL4 project), with Volkswagen and MOIA
operators.statusText: Since Oct 2025; passenger trials delayed (last confirmed Jul 2026)
operators.fleetNote: Five VW ID. Buzz AD minibuses (BVG)
operators.note: Level 4-capable VW ID. Buzz AD vehicles have been tested on public roads in parts of Spandau, Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf and Reinickendorf since Oct 2025, with a safety driver on board and no passengers. Free rides for selected test participants were planned for the first half of 2026; in Jul 2026 BVG told dpa it now aims to start passenger operation “bestenfalls noch in diesem Jahr” (at best, later this year).

operators.fleetNote: Current fleet not stated; PostBus plans regular operation with up to 25 vehicles without safety drivers from 2027
operators.note: Under a special permit from the Federal Roads Office (FEDRO), Apollo RT6 vehicles have driven in automated mode with safety drivers on board since 1 Jun 2026, across an 80 km² area in St. Gallen and the two Appenzell cantons. No customers yet: PostBus’s autumn update (29 Sep 2026) says the booking app for a first test-user group is being developed and tested.

Uber and Momenta announced plans in Sep 2025 for Level 4 testing in Munich in 2026. The KBA’s list of testing approvals (dated 18 Aug 2026) includes a Level 4 approval for Momenta Europe GmbH dated 8 Jul 2026, with no local restriction. On 5 Oct 2026 Uber’s CEO told Handelsblatt that a limited Munich pilot with safety drivers, with partners Momenta and Autobrain, is about to start. We have not found a confirmed start of public-road testing in Munich.

sources.label: KBA list of testing approvals, as of 18 Aug 2026 (German, PDF)
dts news agency via finanznachrichten.de, 5 Oct 2026 (German)

operators.note: Waymo announced on 25 Aug 2026 that its vehicles would start driving manually in Munich to map the city, followed by testing with trained specialists behind the wheel. It aims to open commercial ride-hailing to the public towards the end of 2027, subject to approvals. We have not found confirmation that automated testing has begun.

operators.operator: WeRide with Uber and AVOMO (Moove Cars Group)
operators.statusText: Announced Jun 2026; national test permit 10 Sep 2026
operators.fleetNote: Initial phase of twenty vehicles with an in-car vehicle specialist (WeRide)
operators.note: WeRide and Uber announced in Jun 2026 a commercial robotaxi pilot in the Madrid region, bookable on the Uber app. On 10 Sep 2026 they said Spain’s Directorate General of Traffic (DGT) had granted a national permit for Level 4 vehicles, allowing mapping, route validation and readiness testing. Commercial operations are expected by the end of 2026. We have not found a confirmed start of automated public-road testing.

permits.label: UK driverless passenger permits granted
permits.note: No automated passenger services (APS) permit has been announced. On 1 Oct 2026 Covington’s Global Policy Watch reported that permits for the first automated passenger services were “yet to be granted”, and that as of late September no operator had applied for a driverless permit. In an FOI response published on 4 Sep 2026, TfL said it had received no formal APS consent requests.

changelog.title: Weekly review: six entries added, no status changes
items: No status changes to existing entries; all 11 existing entries re-verified against their sources on 5 Oct 2026.

Added: iamo in the Furttal, Canton of Zurich (Passenger rides with safety driver, since 28 Sep 2026; 3 cars). The project partners say it is the first time passengers in Switzerland can book self-driving vehicles; a safety person sits in the driver’s seat.
Added: Nissan’s ADventure research project in Cambridge (Announced, 27 Sep 2026).

Added four entries we had missed at launch: Greater Cambridge Partnership’s Connector self-driving buses (Passenger rides with safety driver, since Jun 2025), BVG’s NoWeL4 shuttles in Berlin (Testing with safety driver, since Oct 2025), Waymo in Munich (Announced, Aug 2026) and WeRide with Uber in the Madrid region (Announced, Jun 2026; national test permit 10 Sep 2026).
London (Wayve with Uber): fleet now shown as “Up to 15”, the number of vehicles TfL approved for the trial.

Munich (Momenta with Uber): we checked the KBA list of testing approvals, which includes Momenta’s Level 4 approval, and added Uber’s 5 Oct 2026 statement that a pilot with safety drivers is about to start. Status stays at Announced.
Hamburg (MOIA): added a press report that Volkswagen is reviewing MOIA’s future. Oslo (Ruter): still no confirmed restart.
UK driverless passenger permits granted: still 0.

changelog.title: Baseline: tracker launched
items: First version of the tracker, with 11 operator–city entries (5 UK, 6 elsewhere in Europe), each checked against the linked sources on 4 Oct 2026.
Not yet confirmed: whether Ruter’s Oslo pilot has restarted, whether beti’s Drôme shuttle has run since April 2026, and when Uber’s own Apollo Go testing in London began.
